constraint_decided_it: P94 has created: scope note 'It does not represent the act of creating the first physical carrier ... this is the composition of a poem, not its commitment to paper', plus quantification 'one to many, necessary, dependent (1,n:1,1)'. B routes the secretary's signing of the sheets through a second E65 Creation with P94 has created -> E34 Inscription. Signing is precisely commitment to paper, which that clause excludes; and the (1,1) range dependency means an E28 is created by exactly one E65, so a signature prototype cannot be P94-created afresh by each signing event across a bundle of letters. E34's own scope note compounds it: the class is 'not intended to describe the idiosyncratic characteristics of an individual physical embodiment of an inscription, but the underlying prototype'. A instead records the signature as E22 P65 shows visual item -> E37 Mark, which is domain/range clean (P65: E24 -> E36; E22 subclass of E24, E37 subclass of E36) and matches E37's scope note verbatim: 'symbols, signs, signatures, or short texts applied to instances of E24 Physical Human-Made Thing ... in order to indicate such things as creator, owner'.
better_modelling: Composition: E65 Creation, P94 has created -> E33 Linguistic Object, P14 carried out by -> the drafter with P14.1 in the role of -> 'drafter' (E55). Neither answer names P14.1, although P14's own scope note ('The P14.1 in the role of property of the property specifies the nature of an Actor's participation') and its FOL clause P14(x,y,z) => [P14(x,y) AND E55(z)] provide exactly this role split; both only gesture at 'roles'. Carrier: the letter E22 P128 carries -> the E33 text (B has this, A omits any link between text and object) and P65 shows visual item -> the E37/E34 signature. Signing: not an E65 Creation but an E11 Modification (or E12 Production, whose scope note gives 'the scribbling of a name on a potsherd may make it a voting token'), P31 has modified -> the E22 letter, P14 carried out by -> the secretary, P14.1 in the role of -> 'signatory'. Uncertainty: E13 Attribute Assignment, P140 assigned attribute to -> the E65 Creation, P141 assigned -> the unnamed E21 Person, P177 assigned property of type -> P14 as E55, P14 carried out by -> the cataloguer, P3 has note for the handwriting/letterhead evidence.
reasoning: Both reach the same core modelling (E65/P94 -> E33 for composition, E13 reification for the cataloguer's inference), so the split is in the details. B is the more complete of the two -- it alone supplies P128 carries, names the cataloguer as the E13's actor, and supplies P177 assigned property of type, whose quantification (1,n:0,n) is 'necessary' and which A's E13 omits -- and its P94 quotation is verbatim against the scope note. But B then applies P94 to the act B itself describes as 'signing the sheet', which the sentence it quotes explicitly excludes, and the (1,1) range dependency plus E34's prototype clause forbid the pattern across a bundle. B also mischaracterises two cited threads: t1300 ended by retaining 'signatures' in E37's revised scope note (Doerr: 'E37 is about the process of generation. E34 is about the content following the process'), so it does not support B's rejection of E37 for a signature; and t1477 floats a new subproperty Pxx_carried_out_by_member_or_members_of while stating 'This doesn't seem like a use for P14.1', contradicting B's 'a possible P14.1-style property floated'. A's thread claims check out (t0796, t1477, t1345-adjacent, and t1704/t0840/t1035 are genuinely CRMinf belief threads), it paraphrases rather than fabricates the P94 wording, and it commits no domain/range or scope-note violation -- but it omits the necessary P177, never links the E22 to the E33, never assigns an actor to the signing at all, and one sentence dangles the 'conceiving vs. committing to paper' scope note off P14 rather than P94 (corrected in its rejected alternatives). Omitting a required property is a lesser fault than asserting a relation the property's own scope note forbids, so A wins narrowly.
